I'm working on a commercial webapp using Lean. As I'm going along, I've been breaking out anything generic (not specific to the application's business logic) into a library. I recently hit the milestone of having everything necessary to support a complete production webapp.

To that end, I've created a demo, based on the traditional TodoMVC, but extended to include passwordless sign-in, SQL migrations, telemetry, an LLM assistant panel, and IaC deployment to AWS Lambda.

https://github.com/paulbutcher/lean-todomvc-max

The stack it's built upon is:
lean-html · lean-htmx typed markup and typed hx-* attributes
lean-routing typed router and route table
lean-middleware sessions, sealed cookie store, anti-forgery, static files, request tracing
lean-authentication magic links, sessions, rate limiting, bounce handling, consent
leanpostgres · leanmigrate libpq bindings with a connection pool; migrations as plain SQL files
lean-telemetry OpenTelemetry traces and logs
lean-llmclient · lean-markdown provider-agnostic chat with tool calling; GFM for rendering replies
lean-aws · lean-aws-lambda SigV4 signing; the Lambda runtime interface
lean-json JSON (see below)
leancurl libcurl bindings
leancrypto SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, RSA verification, codecs, DER

The obvious question is why a new JSON library rather than Lean.Data.Json.

The deployed binary is ~12 MB; Lean.Data.Json is part of the compiler frontend and linking that frontend would increase the binary size by ~125MB, increasing cold start times from the current ~2 seconds to ~15 seconds.

lean-json provides some stronger guarantees than Lean.Data.Json: nothing in it is partial, nothing can panic, it is proved correct against the grammar of RFC 8259, and no operation walks a value on the C stack, so a deeply nested document is a bounded error rather than a crash. Codecs, paths, deriving ToJson, FromJson and json% literals are all there; see its README.
So cool! If you're looking for contributors/collaborators on any of these let me know. I'd like to make something in this space as well
I am looking forward to read some testimonials!

@Valentin Erokhin Thanks for the kind words. Initially at least, it would be great if you could build/deploy the application following the instructions and let me know if you hit any issues along the way (so I can fix the instructions if necessary).

Hello, did not read all, but i reviewed some parts of Middleware.

  • The multipart one does a one time read, meaning that uploading gigabyte files will all end up in memory for parsing. You could use streaming. You can take a look at what i did for LeanIO/MultiPart where everything is streamed and parsed on the fly with a zero copy chuncked buffer.
  • The File one does not handle the Range protocol, this one is handy for resumability and streaming video/audio chunks and seeking. you can see here how it's handled in LeanIO/RangeFile

I can also do a review of the other libraries if you want to. Would be happy to help.

Other feedback for the Router :

  • it currently does a linear search (performance for dispatching will degrade as program grows)
  • there is no standard router dispatching priority, the first matching handler wins.

A solution is to use a two step router. The declarative part and the compiled part that transform the router into a RouteTrie. This will make the dispatch become O(Depth) instead of O(Length). And with a bonus to have naturally dispatching priority backed in Again you can take a look at LeanIO/RouteTrie for inspiration.
I wonder if something like https://github.com/frangio/thyme can be used for the router

Hi Paul, there is some nice stuff here, congratulations, and welcome. :-)

I have only looked closely at the "bottom" layer, your leancrypto library, which seems ... quite good!

A while back (in the early days, when AI was first becoming useful), I wrote my own lean-crypto-hash library. Goaded by your announcement, I've just made some updates to mine (sometimes unashamedly imitating!) and I wonder if we should coordinate to make something reliable and durable.

Both libraries implement SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, and hexadecimal encoding and decoding. Both have basic conformance tests, and somewhat different coverage of basic theorems about encoding/decoding operations.

lean-crypto-hash has many more hashing algorithms: MD5, SHA-1, all standard SHA-2 and SHA-3 variants, SHAKE128/256, and four SHA-2 HMAC variants. Significantly, if also provides GNU-compatible checksum command-line tools, and quite extensive conformance testing against NIST vectors, OpenSSL, and GNU coreutils.

Your leancrypto extends in other great directions beyond hashing:

  • Base64, Base64URL, and Crockford Base32 codecs,
  • RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 signature verification
  • limited DER, X.509, and PEM processing for extracting RSA public keys

What would you say to combining/extending/opening up to others these basic bits? (err... someone should probably do a literature search to see what else is already out there!)

How about:

  • We move out all the codec stuff (hexadecimal, and BaseX) to a separate lean-crypto-codec
  • We see if we can have your library essentially depend on mine for SHA-256?
  • We rename your additional material to lean-crypto-rsa

Good to hear from you Kim, and thank you for the kind words.

FYI (so you understand how I've got to where I've got to) my primary motivation is that I'm working on a private application (the source of which isn't and won't be published), but I'm splitting out and publishing anything generic as/when I get to it.

So leancrypto supports precisely that subset of the crypto world my application happens to need today (the same general caveat applies to all the other libraries mentioned above).

That notwithstanding, I would be delighted to combine as you suggest. Do you have a plan of attack in mind? I'm not at all precious about ownership: I wouldn't have written it at all if I already had access to something that did what I needed, so as long as we end up with something that provides the same (or better) functionality and the same (or better) guarantees, I will be happy :blush:
